patterns_that_work: Observed: on LinkedIn, human posts beat product posts by a wide margin. Motion's culture post (3,154 likes), meme (538) and named-practitioner workflow (316) versus 14 to 32 likes for its product, report and event posts.

Observed: templated or automated daily posts fail. Segwise's 'If you want to know...' posts got 0 to 4 likes on a 16k-follower page; Foreplay's 'Found on Foreplay' daily series got 0 to 3 likes and stopped at #225.
Observed: follower count does not predict engagement. Segwise (16.2k) and GoMarble (7.7k) get less per post than Hawky (4.5k).

Observed: vendor-written 'best tools' and 'X vs Y' pages own the category search results (Segwise had 7 of the top 20 links for the DTC creative analytics query; Hawky ranks itself first for the India query).
Observed: original data earns press. Motion's Creative Benchmarks report was covered by trade press and is quoted by rivals.
Observed: borrowed reach through guests. Hawky's podcast pull-quote posts are its best-performing LinkedIn format (10 to 24 likes).
Observed: free tools are standard top-of-funnel (Hawky 14 tools, Foreplay Chrome extension, Triple Whale benchmarks, Segwise tag generator, AdGraam calculators).
Observed: nearly everyone shipped an MCP or 'agent' in 2026 (Motion/Runneth, Atria, Foreplay, Segwise, GoMarble, Hawky). 'Agent' is now table stakes language, not a differentiator.
Inferred: the US players grow through a named identity ('creative strategist') plus community furniture (newsletter, events, university), not through feature posts.
whitespace_for_galvor: Buyer voice: no competitor leads with reading comments and reviews on the brand's own ads. Atria and Runneth mention reviews as a research input; nobody makes it the headline.

Pure 'why it wins' intelligence: Hawky, GoMarble, Motion and Atria have all moved toward agents that launch and manage ads. A read-only tool that explains patterns in plain language is now less crowded.
India D2C teardown content: Hawky's Decoding series has been quiet since 16 Jul 2026. A consistent weekly Decoded can own this.
An India D2C creative benchmarks report: Motion does this for the US; no Indian equivalent was found.
Plain rupee pricing or a free first look: Hawky hides price; the US tools start at $125 to $999 a month in dollars; only AdGraam publishes rupee prices.
Human, founder-and-practitioner-led LinkedIn: every India-linked competitor's feed is either guest clips or product pitch with low engagement.
Newsletter: neither Hawky, Segwise, AdGraam nor GoMarble shows a newsletter; Motion's Thumbstop is the only strong one and it is US-focused.
Simple vocabulary (format, story, reason to buy): competitors talk in hooks, tags, agents and MCPs. The plain-language framing is distinct.
watch_list: Hawky: whether it keeps drifting to media buying or returns to creative intelligence; whether Decoding restarts; any funding news
Motion's Runneth: it already claims concepting from customer reviews and comments; watch for an India push or a cheaper tier
Canva Grow: AI ad tagging inside Canva could make basic creative analysis free for small teams
AdGraam: newly funded, India D2C, rupee pricing; watch whether its analytics deepens
Segwise: pushing hard from gaming into DTC with Indian D2C logos already
Pixis and QuickAds: India-linked, not yet overlapping, could move closer
Atria: review mining plus low price; watch for international or India pricing
